title: Fruit boat, New York, Johnson boys and coming to California in 1915
summary: Working on the United Fruit boat, meeting the Johnson boys, and settling in Los Angeles in 1915.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When you first came to California, do you remember about what year was there or did you go on the road first? You said to New York someplace before you came here?

No, out of school, yes. I worked for the United Fruit Company boat. Oh, yeah. Yeah. And that's how I got to New York. So, I got with those Johnson boys, as I said. Let's see, one was a guitar player and the other was a bass player. Did you know them? The Johnsons?

Well, there's so many Johnsons. Is that Bill Johnson, you think? No, no, no, no. Wasn't that bunch? No, Bill Johnson from Monk. From out here. The bass player, yeah. He was out here already. That's why I remember him.
Johnson. He was at Dunbar's Tennessee Tanks, too. Well, yeah, that's when I got out here, but I didn't go back, see?
When did you first come to California?
1915 when they had the bass here.
1915 you came here? Yeah. Somebody told me the other day they thought you came here in 1912, but that wasn't right.
Yeah, somebody told me the other day, I don't know who it was, it doesn't make any difference, but you've been here ever since 1912. No, they got to mix up.

I came here in 1915, and I didn't go back with them. I lived in Los Angeles all that time. Then when I got discharged here in San Francisco, I had a job over here, they used to call it the Barber Coast. Now they call it the International. Yeah. So I worked over there with another old guy from New Orleans. He never did go back. He might have left there in 1912. His name is Sid Leprotti.
